div.div: watchfloor: CI/CD and who can change what

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1178px; height: 1px; padding-top: 42px; margin-left: 2px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #545B64;
display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#545B64, #9aa0a8); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: No AWS keys are stored in GitHub. Every job that touches AWS asks GitHub for a short-lived OIDC token, and AWS only trades it for credentials if aud = sts.amazonaws.com and sub matches the pattern pinned on that role. Each workflow gets its own role. terraform-bootstrap and terraform-persistent are applied by hand; CI only ever applies the terraform/ app stack.

div.div:
Permissions boundary: watchfloor-app-boundary
Every role the apply role creates must carry it. It caps those roles at: pulling images, reading SSM parameters, getting a web identity token, writing logs, publishing to watchfloor-* SNS topics, and the SSM tunnel channels.
No IAM writes and no assuming other roles. The apply role is explicitly denied from removing the boundary from a role or editing the boundary policy itself.
